 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Zakye Barker had just left campus after his recruiting visit to North Texas a few months ago when coach Neal Brown stopped Bradley Dale Peveto to talk.
 UNT was in the middle of a massive rebuilding project that saw the Mean Green bring in more than 70 new players and upward of 50 transfers. The level of turnover would require UNT to find a new batch of leaders, and Brown was convinced the Mean Green had found one in Barker.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "He's super impressive and very mature. I told coach Peveto when he left, 'This kid's going to be a difference-maker,'" Brown said of his conversation with his co-defensive coordinator and linebackers coach.
 That's exactly what Barker has been for UNT, which will need him to be at his best again Saturday, when the Mean Green face one of their biggest challenges of the season.
 UNT has run out to a 7-2 start, won six straight games and moved to the top of the American Conference standings at 5-0. UTSA is lurking a game back at 4-1 after also starting 7-2, while Memphis is 5-1 in league play after beating South Florida on Thursday night.
 A win over UTSA would inch UNT closer to earning a trip to the American title game for the second straight season, not to mention give the Mean Green a win over their biggest rival.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Brown feels a whole lot better about UNT's prospects against the Roadrunners with Barker helping lead the way.
 "Our leadership has been really good," Brown said. "We've got guys who have played football, but don't necessarily have a ton of guys who have played a lot of meaningful football this late into the season."
 Barker is among the few, along with quarterback Tayven Jackson, offensive lineman Chandler Strong and a handful of others.
 UNT has leaned on those veterans throughout the season and will again on Saturday.
 "You're only as good as your connections," Barker said. "We've been really good making those connections. We know how to play winning football because we've all been on winning teams before."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Barker certainly has that type of experience. He was East Carolina's second-leading tackler with 86 stops in 2024, when the Pirates finished 8-5 and beat North Carolina State in the Military Bowl.
 "We thought he'd be one of our top guys," Brown said. "He's super impressive and very mature. When you have a recruit come in, one of the things I pay attention to is what type of questions they ask.
 "Zakye is a veteran and asked quality questions."
 He quickly joined a handful of players who set the tone for UNT as a result while also producing on the field. He's by far the Mean Green's leading tackler with 72 stops, a total that ranks among the top 10 in the American and is a dozen more than safety CJ Coombes among UNT players.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The challenge for UNT will be to carry over the way it has played behind Barker, Jackson and a few other veterans in what has developed into a key rivalry with UTSA.
 The teams have played a series of consequential and often thrilling games over the years. One memorable meeting between the teams came in 2017, when Mason Fine guided UNT on a 98-yard, game-winning touchdown drive in the final 67 seconds.
 UTSA returned the favor in 2022, when Frank Harris led a touchdown drive in the closing seconds to pull out a game at the Alamodome, where the Roadrunners beat the Mean Green in the Conference USA championship game a few weeks later.
 "There's a ton of history behind the game," Strong said. "It's a great opportunity."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Beating UTSA would certainly be a landmark win for UNT for a host of reasons. The Mean Green haven't won at the Alamodome since 2018 and are 1-6 in the venue all-time.
 UNT had lost four straight games in the series before hammering UTSA 55-17 last season.
 The Mean Green are well aware of how difficult it will be to build on that win and knock off UTSA for the second straight season. The Roadrunners are 27-1 at home in conference play since 2020, the year Jeff Traylor took over the program.
 "It's a credit to them, the environment and the fan support they've created there at the Alamodome," Brown said. "It's a huge challenge, not only taking on what is a really good and well-coached football team but also handling the elements."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement UTSA has one of the more experienced quarterbacks in the country in senior Owen McCown, who has started 39 games and thrown for 9,477 yards in his career, including 2,016 this year.
 UNT will counter with its dynamic pairing of quarterback Tayven Jackson and running back Jahiem White. Jackson has thrown for 2,880 yards, while White has rushed for 1,186 yards.
 The pair has UNT headed into the weekend leading the country in total offense with an average of 534.7 yards per game.
 Traylor spoke highly of the job Brown has done rebuilding UNT from the ground up after the departure of Eric Morris, who left for Oklahoma State and took a host of players with him after last season.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "Neal Brown should be considered for every national coaching award there is for what he's done this year," Traylor said. "You don't get to be the No. 1 offense in the country without great players and great coaching."
 Four downs: Keys to today's game
Handle the Alamodome environment
The Alamodome is a tough place for any team to play. UTSA is not only 27-1 in conference games at home since 2020, it's 37-5 overall. The Mean Green are capable of pulling out a win, but they'll have to settle in quickly and play well.
 Get the offense going again
UNT has been terrific all season offensively and has scored at least 45 points in each of its last six games. The Mean Green will be tough to beat if Jackson and White can get UNT's offense rolling again against a UTSA defense that allowed 60 points in a loss to Florida Atlantic last week.
 Contain UTSA QB Owen McCown
Owen McCown is one of the more experienced and productive players in the American. Brown and his players this week praised his toughness as well as the way he manages UTSA's offense. Keeping McCown contained and not allowing him to move around and make plays is critical.
